title: AWS
description: AWS is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform, offering 200+ fully featured services from data centers globally.
variants: 200+ services across 30+ categories
alternatives: Microsoft Azure • Google Cloud Platform
freeTier: 12-month free tier + always-free services + short-term trials
useCases: Store and analyze petabytes of data
devNote: Start with IAM + VPC + EC2/Lambda. These three form the foundation of almost every AWS architecture you'll build.

title: Compute
description: Where your application code runs. The core question: how much infrastructure do you want to manage? VMs give full control; serverless gives zero ops.
variants: VM • Serverless • Containers • Batch
alternatives: Azure Compute • GCP Compute Engine
devNote: Rule of thumb: EC2 for full control, Lambda for event-driven, ECS/Fargate for containers. Start with Lambda for new projects.

title: EC2
description: Elastic Compute Cloud — rent a virtual server in AWS. You pick the CPU, RAM, OS, and storage. Full root access. You manage the OS, patches, and runtime.
learn: Imagine renting a computer in AWS's data center. EC2 gives you the machine — you're responsible for everything inside it: OS, runtime, app, patches.
pricing: Per second/hour by instance family and size
variants: t4g (general) • c7g (compute) • r7g (memory) • p4 (GPU) • i4i (storage)
alternatives: Lambda • ECS Fargate • Azure VMs • GCP Compute Engine
devNote: Use EC2 when you need OS-level control, specific runtimes, or persistent long-running processes. Pair with Auto Scaling Groups for production.

title: Lambda
description: Run code in response to events without managing any servers. AWS provisions, scales, and retires the infrastructure automatically. You pay only when code executes.
learn: Think: 'I only care about my function, not the server.' Lambda runs your code and disappears — you never see or touch the machine underneath.
variants: Node.js • Python • Java • Go • Ruby • .NET • Custom Runtime
alternatives: EC2 • ECS Fargate • Azure Functions • Cloud Run
devNote: Lambda cold starts matter for latency-sensitive APIs. Use Provisioned Concurrency for consistent response times. Keep functions small and single-purpose.

title: ECS
description: Elastic Container Service — run Docker containers as tasks and services. AWS manages the control plane. You choose EC2 or Fargate for the data plane.
learn: If your app is a Docker container, ECS keeps the desired number of containers running, handles restarts, and manages placement across hosts.
pricing: No charge for ECS itself — pay for underlying EC2 or Fargate
variants: EC2 launch type (you manage instances) • Fargate launch type (serverless)
alternatives: EKS (Kubernetes) • Azure AKS • Google GKE
freeTier: No ECS charge — pay for compute resources
devNote: ECS is simpler than EKS. Use ECS + Fargate for most container workloads unless you specifically need Kubernetes ecosystem tools.

title: Fargate
description: Serverless compute engine for containers. Run ECS or EKS pods without provisioning or managing EC2 instances. AWS handles all server infrastructure.
learn: Fargate is to containers what Lambda is to functions — you bring the image, AWS handles the rest. No SSH, no patching, no capacity planning.
variants: ECS on Fargate • EKS on Fargate • Fargate Spot (up to 70% cheaper)
alternatives: EC2 launch type • Lambda • Cloud Run
freeTier: No free tier — pay per use
devNote: Fargate Spot is great for fault-tolerant batch jobs at 70% discount. For production APIs, use standard Fargate with task auto-scaling.

title: Storage
description: Where files, objects, disks, and shared file systems live. Match the storage type to your access pattern: object for files, block for disks, file for shared mounts.
variants: Object • Block • File • Archive
alternatives: Azure Storage • Google Cloud Storage
devNote: S3 for everything file-like. EBS only for EC2 disks. EFS when multiple instances need the same files. Glacier for cold archival.

title: S3
description: Simple Storage Service — store any file as an object in a bucket. 11 nines (99.999999999%) of durability. Virtually unlimited capacity. Global access.
learn: S3 is a massive digital warehouse. Store an object in a bucket, retrieve it by key. No folders — just key prefixes that look like paths.
variants: Standard • Intelligent-Tiering • Standard-IA • One Zone-IA • Glacier IR • Glacier FR • Deep Archive
alternatives: EFS • Azure Blob Storage • GCS
devNote: Enable versioning on important buckets. Use lifecycle rules to auto-transition to cheaper tiers. Block public access by default — enable only when needed.

title: EBS
description: Elastic Block Store — a virtual hard drive attached to an EC2 instance. Low-latency block storage for databases, boot volumes, and high-IOPS workloads.
learn: If EC2 is a computer, EBS is its hard drive. It persists when the instance stops. But it's locked to one AZ — can't attach to instances in another AZ.
variants: gp3 (general SSD) • io2 Block Express (high IOPS) • st1 (throughput HDD) • sc1 (cold HDD)
alternatives: EFS • Instance Store • Azure Managed Disks
devNote: gp3 is the default choice — cheaper than gp2 and you can tune IOPS/throughput independently. Use io2 only for databases needing >16K IOPS.

title: EFS
description: Elastic File System — fully managed NFS file system. Multiple EC2 instances, containers, and Lambda functions can mount and access it simultaneously.
learn: EFS is a shared network drive. Many servers read and write the same files simultaneously — unlike EBS which is attached to only one instance at a time.
variants: Standard • Infrequent Access • One Zone • One Zone-IA
alternatives: S3 • EBS • FSx for Windows/Lustre
useCases: Shared content repositories for web farms
Big data analytics with shared access
devNote: EFS scales automatically — no capacity planning needed. Use Intelligent Tiering to auto-move cold files to IA storage and cut costs by 85%.

title: Glacier
description: Ultra-low-cost archival storage for data you rarely access. Part of the S3 storage class family. Retrieval times range from milliseconds to 12 hours.
learn: Glacier is cold storage — extremely cheap but you wait to get data back. Instant Retrieval costs more but returns in milliseconds. Deep Archive is cheapest but takes hours.
variants: Glacier Instant Retrieval (ms) • Glacier Flexible (mins-hrs) • Glacier Deep Archive (hrs)
alternatives: S3 Standard-IA • Azure Archive • Tape backup
devNote: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to Glacier after N days. Vault Lock enforces WORM (write-once-read-many) for compliance.

title: Database
description: Where application data lives. Relational for structured data with relationships. NoSQL for scale and flexibility. In-memory for microsecond latency.
variants: Relational • NoSQL • In-Memory • Graph • Time-Series
alternatives: Self-managed databases • Cloud SQL
devNote: Default to RDS PostgreSQL for relational. DynamoDB for high-scale key-value. ElastiCache in front of any DB to cut latency and cost.

title: RDS
description: Relational Database Service — fully managed SQL database. AWS handles provisioning, patching, backups, failover, and read replicas. You focus on queries.
learn: Choose RDS when your data fits tables, rows, and SQL. AWS handles the boring ops work — backups, patches, failover — so you focus on your schema and queries.
pricing: db.t3.micro ~$0.017/hr • storage $0.115/GB-mo • Multi-AZ doubles instance cost
variants: MySQL • PostgreSQL • MariaDB • Oracle • SQL Server • Db2
alternatives: Aurora • Self-managed on EC2 • Azure SQL • Cloud SQL
devNote: Enable Multi-AZ for production (automatic failover in ~60s). Add Read Replicas for read-heavy workloads. Use Parameter Groups to tune the engine.

title: DynamoDB
description: Managed key-value and document database. Single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Fully serverless — no instances to manage, auto-scales capacity.
learn: DynamoDB is designed around how you read data, not how it's shaped. Get your partition key and sort key right and it scales infinitely. Get them wrong and you'll hit hot partitions.
variants: On-Demand (pay per request) • Provisioned (reserved capacity) • Global Tables (multi-region active-active)
alternatives: RDS • MongoDB Atlas • Azure Cosmos DB
freeTier: 25 GB storage + 25 WCU + 25 RCU — always free
devNote: Design access patterns FIRST, then model your table. A single-table design with composite keys is the DynamoDB way. Use DAX for microsecond caching.

title: Aurora
description: AWS-built relational engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. Up to 5x faster than MySQL, 3x faster than PostgreSQL. Storage auto-scales to 128 TB.
learn: Aurora is what you choose when standard RDS isn't fast or available enough. Same SQL, same drivers — just AWS-engineered storage and replication underneath.
variants: Aurora MySQL • Aurora PostgreSQL • Aurora Serverless v2 • Aurora Global Database
alternatives: RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL • Cloud Spanner • Azure SQL Hyperscale
devNote: Aurora Serverless v2 scales in fine-grained increments (0.5 ACU steps) — great for variable workloads. Global Database gives <1s cross-region replication.

title: ElastiCache
description: Managed in-memory data store supporting Redis and Memcached. Sub-millisecond latency. Dramatically reduces database load for frequently accessed data.
learn: ElastiCache sits in front of your database. Hot data lives in memory and returns in <1ms instead of hitting the DB. Cache-aside pattern: check cache first, fall back to DB.
variants: Redis OSS • Valkey • Memcached • ElastiCache Serverless
alternatives: DAX (for DynamoDB) • Self-managed Redis • Azure Cache for Redis
devNote: Redis is almost always the right choice over Memcached — it supports persistence, replication, Lua scripting, and richer data structures. Use cluster mode for horizontal scale.

title: Networking
description: How users reach your app and how AWS services talk to each other. Learn the path: DNS → VPC → Load Balancer → App. Add CloudFront at the edge.
variants: Network • DNS • Load Balancer • CDN • VPN • Direct Connect
alternatives: Other cloud networking stacks
devNote: Always start with a VPC design. Use private subnets for databases and app servers. Public subnets only for load balancers and NAT gateways.

title: VPC
description: Virtual Private Cloud — your logically isolated network inside AWS. Define IP ranges, subnets, route tables, internet gateways, and security boundaries.
learn: A VPC is your private neighborhood inside AWS. You control the streets (subnets), traffic rules (route tables), gates (internet gateway), and who can enter (security groups).
variants: IPv4 • IPv6 • Dual-stack • VPC Peering • Transit Gateway • PrivateLink
alternatives: Other cloud virtual networks
useCases: Connect on-premises data center to AWS
devNote: Standard 3-tier VPC: public subnet (ALB, NAT GW), private subnet (app servers), isolated subnet (databases). Use Security Groups as stateful firewalls, NACLs for subnet-level rules.

title: Route 53
description: Scalable DNS and domain registration. Translates domain names to IPs and can make intelligent routing decisions based on health, latency, geography, and weight.
learn: When a user types your domain, Route 53 answers: 'Where should this go?' It can also watch your endpoints and reroute traffic if one goes down.
variants: Simple • Weighted • Latency-based • Failover • Geolocation • Geoproximity • Multi-value
alternatives: Cloudflare DNS • Azure DNS • Google Cloud DNS
freeTier: No free tier for hosted zones
useCases: Automatic failover on health check failure
devNote: Use Latency-based routing for global apps to send users to the nearest region. Combine with Health Checks for automatic failover. Alias records are free (unlike CNAME).

title: ELB
description: Elastic Load Balancing — distributes incoming traffic across healthy targets. Decouples clients from servers. Handles SSL termination, sticky sessions, and health checks.
learn: A load balancer is the traffic controller in front of your servers. It checks which servers are healthy and distributes each request to one of them.
variants: ALB (HTTP/HTTPS, Layer 7) • NLB (TCP/UDP, Layer 4) • GWLB (network appliances)
alternatives: Nginx • HAProxy • Azure Load Balancer • GCP Load Balancing
useCases: Distribute web traffic across EC2 fleet
Inline traffic inspection with security appliances (GWLB)
devNote: Use ALB for HTTP/HTTPS apps — it supports path routing, host routing, and Lambda targets. Use NLB for ultra-low latency or non-HTTP protocols. ALB + WAF is the standard web security combo.

title: CloudFront
description: Global Content Delivery Network with 450+ edge locations worldwide. Caches content at the edge closest to users. Reduces latency, origin load, and data transfer costs.
learn: CloudFront puts copies of your content at 450+ locations worldwide. Users download from the nearest edge — 50ms instead of 300ms to a distant origin.
variants: Web distributions • Origin Shield • Lambda@Edge • CloudFront Functions
alternatives: Cloudflare • Fastly • Akamai • Azure CDN
freeTier: 1 TB data transfer out + 10M HTTP/HTTPS requests/mo — 12 months
useCases: Accelerate static website and SPA delivery
Video streaming with low global latency
DDoS protection at the edge (with Shield)
devNote: Use Origin Shield as an extra caching layer to reduce origin hits by 60-80%. CloudFront Functions run in <1ms for simple header manipulation. Lambda@Edge for complex logic.

title: Security
description: Who can access what, how data is encrypted, how threats are detected, and how web applications are protected. Security is everyone's job in AWS.
variants: Identity • Encryption • Firewall • Threat Detection • Compliance
alternatives: Third-party security tools
useCases: Control access to all AWS resources
Encrypt data at rest and in transit
Protect web apps from OWASP Top 10
devNote: Security is not optional. Enable MFA on root account immediately. Use IAM roles (not users) for applications. Enable GuardDuty in every account and region.

title: IAM
description: Identity and Access Management — the foundation of AWS security. Controls who (users, roles, services) can perform which actions on which resources.
learn: Authentication = 'Who are you?' Authorization = 'What can you do?' IAM answers both. A policy is a JSON document that says: allow/deny this action on this resource.
pricing: No extra charge — included with every AWS account
variants: IAM Users • IAM Groups • IAM Roles • Managed Policies • Inline Policies • Identity Center (SSO)
alternatives: AWS Cognito • External IdP (Okta, Azure AD)
freeTier: Always free — no limits on IAM usage
useCases: Allow EC2 instances to access S3 without credentials
Federate corporate Active Directory to AWS
Enforce MFA for console and API access
devNote: Never use root account for daily work. Never embed access keys in code — use IAM roles. Follow least-privilege: start with no permissions, add only what's needed. Use IAM Access Analyzer to find overly permissive policies.

title: KMS
description: Key Management Service — create, store, rotate, and control cryptographic keys. Integrated with 100+ AWS services for seamless encryption at rest.
learn: KMS is the control room for encryption keys. Most AWS services have a checkbox: 'Encrypt with KMS.' Check it. KMS handles key storage, rotation, and access control.
pricing: $1/mo per customer managed key + $0.03 per 10K API calls
variants: AWS Managed Keys (free) • Customer Managed Keys (CMK) • Custom Key Store (CloudHSM)
alternatives: CloudHSM • HashiCorp Vault • Azure Key Vault
useCases: Audit all key usage via CloudTrail
devNote: Use AWS Managed Keys for simplicity (free, auto-rotated). Use CMKs when you need key policy control or cross-account access. Enable automatic annual rotation on all CMKs.

title: WAF
description: Web Application Firewall — inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests and blocks attacks like SQL injection, XSS, and bot traffic before they reach your application.
learn: WAF sits in the request path and asks: 'Does this HTTP request match any bad patterns?' If yes, it blocks it before it ever reaches your app server.
pricing: $5/mo per Web ACL + $1/mo per rule + $0.60/M requests
variants: Managed Rule Groups (AWS + Marketplace) • Custom Rules • Bot Control • Fraud Control
alternatives: Cloudflare WAF • ModSecurity • Azure Front Door WAF
useCases: Rate-limit API endpoints to prevent abuse
Block malicious IPs and known bad actors
devNote: Start with AWS Managed Rules (Core Rule Set + Known Bad Inputs). Add rate-based rules for DDoS mitigation. Use count mode first to see what would be blocked before switching to block.

title: GuardDuty
description: Intelligent threat detection using ML, anomaly detection, and threat intelligence. Continuously monitors CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs for suspicious activity.
learn: GuardDuty watches your AWS logs 24/7 and raises alerts when it detects suspicious behavior — like an EC2 instance suddenly talking to a known malware C2 server.
pricing: Per GB of analyzed log data — CloudTrail ~$4/M events
variants: Standard • EKS Protection • S3 Protection • Malware Protection • RDS Protection • Lambda Protection
alternatives: AWS Security Hub • Splunk • Datadog Security
useCases: Identify unusual API calls from stolen credentials
Detect port scanning and brute force attacks
devNote: Enable GuardDuty in every account and every region — it's cheap and catches real attacks. Integrate with Security Hub for centralized findings. Use EventBridge to auto-remediate findings.

title: AI & ML
description: Build, train, and deploy ML models or call pre-built AI APIs. From foundation models (Bedrock) to full ML pipelines (SageMaker) to vision and language APIs.
variants: Foundation Models • Custom ML • Pre-built AI APIs • No-code ML
alternatives: Azure AI • Google Vertex AI • OpenAI
freeTier: Q Developer free tier • Rekognition 5K images/mo (12mo)
useCases: Custom ML model training and deployment
devNote: Start with Bedrock for GenAI — no infrastructure. Use SageMaker when you need custom model training. Use pre-built APIs (Rekognition, Comprehend, Translate) for common tasks.

title: Bedrock
description: Serverless access to foundation models from Amazon, Anthropic (Claude), Meta (Llama), Mistral, Stability AI, and others via a single unified API.
learn: Bedrock = call powerful AI models via API. No GPUs, no model hosting. You send a prompt, get a response. Pick the model that fits your use case and budget.
pricing: Claude 3 Sonnet: $0.003/1K input tokens + $0.015/1K output tokens
variants: Claude 3 (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) • Llama 3 • Amazon Titan • Mistral • Stable Diffusion • Cohere
alternatives: Azure OpenAI Service • Vertex AI • OpenAI API • Anthropic API
useCases: AI chatbots and customer service automation
devNote: Use Knowledge Bases for RAG — it handles chunking, embedding, and vector search automatically. Use Guardrails to filter harmful content. Agents can call your APIs autonomously.

title: SageMaker
description: End-to-end ML platform covering the full lifecycle: data prep, feature engineering, model training, experiment tracking, deployment, and monitoring.
learn: SageMaker is the full ML workshop. You bring data and model code; SageMaker provides managed compute, experiment tracking, hyperparameter tuning, and deployment.
variants: Studio • Training Jobs • Real-time Endpoints • Batch Transform • Pipelines • Canvas (no-code) • JumpStart
alternatives: Google Vertex AI • Azure ML • Databricks • MLflow
freeTier: SageMaker Studio Lab (free) • 2-month trial for Studio
useCases: Train custom deep learning models at scale
Feature store for shared ML features
devNote: Use Spot Instances for training to cut costs by 70-90%. Use SageMaker JumpStart for pre-built model templates. Use Pipelines for reproducible ML workflows.

title: Amazon Q
description: AI-powered assistant for developers and business users. Q Developer writes, explains, and debugs code in your IDE. Q Business answers questions from your company's data.
learn: Amazon Q Developer is your AI pair programmer. It sees your code context and suggests completions, explains what code does, and can refactor entire files.
pricing: Q Developer Free: free • Q Developer Pro: $19/user/mo • Q Business: $20/user/mo
variants: Q Developer (IDE + CLI) • Q Business (enterprise) • Q in QuickSight • Q in Connect
alternatives: GitHub Copilot • Cursor • ChatGPT • Gemini Code Assist
freeTier: Q Developer free tier: code completions + chat (limited)
useCases: AI code completion and generation in IDE
Answer questions from internal wikis and docs
devNote: Q Developer can scan your code for security vulnerabilities (free). The /transform feature can upgrade Java 8 → Java 17 automatically. Use Q in the CLI for AWS command suggestions.

title: Rekognition
description: Pre-trained computer vision API. Detect objects, scenes, faces, text, and inappropriate content in images and videos. No ML expertise required.
learn: Rekognition is a pre-trained vision model you call via API. Send an image URL, get back structured JSON with labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes.
variants: Image Analysis • Video Analysis • Custom Labels • Face Liveness • Celebrity Recognition
alternatives: Azure Computer Vision • Google Vision AI • Clarifai
useCases: Object and scene detection in images
devNote: Custom Labels lets you train Rekognition on your own images with minimal data (10-20 images per class). Face Liveness detects spoofing attempts for auth flows.

title: Analytics
description: Collect, process, store, and visualize data at any scale. From serverless SQL on S3 to petabyte warehouses to real-time streaming pipelines.
variants: Serverless SQL • Data Warehouse • ETL • Streaming • BI
alternatives: Databricks • Snowflake • BigQuery
useCases: Query S3 data lake with SQL
ETL pipelines from source to warehouse
devNote: Standard data lake pattern: raw data in S3 → Glue crawlers catalog it → Athena for ad-hoc SQL → Redshift for BI dashboards. Add Kinesis for real-time ingestion.

title: Athena
description: Interactive query service — run standard SQL directly on data in S3. No servers, no clusters, no loading data. Pay only for the bytes scanned per query.
learn: Athena is SQL directly on S3. Point it at a folder of files, write SELECT, get results. No database to set up, no data to load. You pay per query.
pricing: $5 per TB of data scanned (use Parquet to cut costs 10x)
variants: Standard SQL • Federated Query (query RDS, DynamoDB, etc.) • Spark (notebooks)
alternatives: Redshift Spectrum • BigQuery • Presto • Trino
useCases: Ad-hoc analysis of S3 data lake
Federated queries across multiple data sources
devNote: Convert CSV to Parquet with Glue to reduce query costs by 87% and speed up queries 34x. Partition your data by date/region to minimize bytes scanned. Use workgroups to control costs per team.

title: Redshift
description: Petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse using columnar storage and massively parallel processing (MPP). Optimized for complex analytical queries across billions of rows.
learn: Redshift answers big analytical questions: 'What were total sales by region for the last 5 years?' It's built for reads across billions of rows, not for transactional writes.
variants: RA3 nodes (managed storage) • Serverless • Redshift Spectrum (query S3) • Data Sharing
alternatives: Snowflake • BigQuery • Azure Synapse Analytics • Databricks
useCases: Historical trend analysis across years of data
Combining data from multiple operational databases
ML predictions with Redshift ML (SageMaker integration)
devNote: Use Redshift Serverless for variable workloads — it scales to zero. Use COPY command (not INSERT) for bulk loading. Sort keys and distribution keys dramatically affect query performance.

title: Glue
description: Serverless data integration service. Discover, catalog, clean, and transform data for analytics and ML. Includes a central Data Catalog used by Athena, Redshift, and EMR.
learn: Glue is the plumber of your data platform. Extract from sources, transform (clean, reshape, join), load into destinations. The Data Catalog is the shared schema registry.
pricing: $0.44/DPU-hr for ETL jobs • $1/100K objects in Data Catalog
variants: Glue ETL (Spark) • Glue Studio (visual) • Data Catalog • DataBrew (no-code) • Glue Streaming
alternatives: AWS Data Pipeline • Apache Spark on EMR • dbt • Fivetran
useCases: Transform raw S3 data into Parquet for Athena
Load and transform data into Redshift
Catalog all data sources in one place
Streaming ETL from Kinesis to S3
devNote: Use Glue Crawlers to auto-discover schema from S3, RDS, and DynamoDB. Use Glue Studio for visual ETL without writing Spark code. Enable job bookmarks to process only new data.

title: Kinesis
description: Collect, process, and analyze real-time streaming data at any scale. Four services covering ingestion, delivery, analytics, and video streaming.
learn: Kinesis is the highway for real-time data. Events flow in continuously and you process them immediately — unlike batch jobs that wait to accumulate data first.
variants: Kinesis Data Streams (custom processing) • Kinesis Firehose (delivery) • Kinesis Data Analytics (SQL/Flink) • Kinesis Video Streams
alternatives: Apache Kafka • Amazon MSK • Azure Event Hubs • Google Pub/Sub
useCases: Real-time clickstream and user behavior analytics
Application log ingestion and delivery to S3
Live video stream ingestion and processing
devNote: Kinesis Firehose is the easiest path — it auto-scales, buffers, and delivers to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch with zero code. Use Data Streams when you need custom consumers or replay.

title: App Integration
description: Connect services using messaging, queuing, and workflow orchestration. Build loosely coupled architectures where services don't need to know about each other.
variants: Queue • Pub/Sub • Workflow • Event Bus
alternatives: RabbitMQ • Kafka • Azure Service Bus
freeTier: SQS 1M req/mo • SNS 1M req/mo • Step Functions 4K transitions/mo — always free
devNote: SQS for point-to-point decoupling. SNS for fan-out. EventBridge for event routing. Step Functions for complex workflows with retries and error handling.

title: SQS
description: Simple Queue Service — fully managed message queue. Producers send messages; consumers poll and process them independently. Decouples services completely.
learn: SQS is a buffer between services. Producer drops a message in the queue; consumer picks it up when ready. They never talk directly — the queue absorbs traffic spikes.
pricing: Standard: $0.40/M requests • FIFO: $0.50/M requests (first 1M free always)
variants: Standard Queue (at-least-once, best-effort order) • FIFO Queue (exactly-once, strict order)
alternatives: RabbitMQ • Azure Service Bus • Google Pub/Sub
useCases: Decouple order placement from order fulfillment
Fan-out with SNS → multiple SQS queues
Dead-letter queues for failed message analysis
devNote: Set visibility timeout > your processing time to prevent duplicate processing. Use DLQ (Dead Letter Queue) to capture failed messages for debugging. Long polling (20s) reduces empty receives and cost.

title: SNS
description: Simple Notification Service — publish one message to a topic and deliver it simultaneously to all subscribers: SQS queues, Lambda functions, HTTP endpoints, email, SMS.
learn: SNS is the megaphone. Publish one message to a topic and SNS delivers it to all subscribers at once — SQS queues, Lambda functions, emails, SMS — simultaneously.
variants: Standard Topics • FIFO Topics • Mobile Push (APNs, FCM) • SMS • Email
alternatives: SQS • EventBridge • Azure Event Grid
useCases: Fan-out to multiple SQS queues simultaneously
Send SMS/email alerts on system events
Trigger multiple Lambda functions from one event
devNote: SNS + SQS fan-out pattern: one SNS topic → multiple SQS queues. Each queue has its own consumer. Message filtering lets subscribers receive only relevant messages.

title: Step Functions
description: Visual workflow service using state machines to coordinate distributed services. Handles retries, error catching, parallel execution, and human approval steps.
learn: Step Functions is the conductor of your microservices orchestra. It defines the sequence, handles failures with retries, and gives you a visual execution map for every run.
pricing: Standard: $0.025/1K state transitions • Express: $1/M transitions + duration
variants: Standard Workflows (long-running, auditable) • Express Workflows (high-volume, short-duration)
alternatives: Apache Airflow • Azure Logic Apps • Temporal • Conductor
useCases: Order processing pipelines (validate → charge → fulfill → notify)
Microservice saga pattern for distributed transactions
devNote: Use SDK Integrations (optimistic) to call AWS services directly without Lambda wrappers — saves cost and latency. Use Express Workflows for high-volume short tasks (IoT, streaming).

title: EventBridge
description: Serverless event bus connecting AWS services, SaaS applications, and custom apps. Route events based on content rules to targets like Lambda, SQS, Step Functions, and more.
learn: EventBridge is the smart event router. When something happens anywhere in your system, EventBridge matches it to rules and sends it to the right handler — no polling needed.
variants: Default Event Bus • Custom Event Bus • Partner Event Sources (Salesforce, Zendesk, etc.) • EventBridge Pipes • Scheduler
alternatives: SNS • Apache Kafka • Azure Event Grid • Pub/Sub
freeTier: No free tier for custom events
useCases: React to AWS service events (EC2 state change, S3 upload)
Integrate SaaS apps without custom code
devNote: EventBridge Scheduler replaces CloudWatch Events for cron jobs — more flexible and reliable. Use Pipes for point-to-point integrations with filtering and enrichment built in.
